header='''# BMW NEXT — Product Specification and Technical Design

**Status:** Hackathon prototype specification · 10 October 2026  
**Context:** TUM AI Hackathon — BMW Challenge, Munich (team-provided brief)  
**Product principle:** AI analyzes. AI challenges. AI explains. Humans decide.

This document is the complete team product brief, followed by implementation contracts and integration guidance. Challenge descriptions and dataset names below are supplied by the team; their contents have not been independently inspected. No real BMW datasets or licensed BMW vehicle assets were present in the repository at project initialization. All initial application evidence is synthetic and must be marked DEMO. This is an unofficial hackathon concept.

The product requirements below are authoritative. The frontend visual specification is retained in full. Implementation choices and open questions follow them; recommendations do not imply that a production backend, real inference, or retrieval security exists in the prototype.

append='''
---

# Implementation Design and Team Interfaces

## System architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  PM[Product manager] --> UI[React + TypeScript frontend]
  UI --> API[Typed IntelligenceService boundary]
  API --> MOCK[Deterministic demo adapter / browser persistence]
  API -. future adapter .-> BACK[Backend API / authentication / authorization]
  ING[Restricted ingestion / cleaning / deduplication] --> DB[(Evidence + source database)]
  DB --> CR[Customer retrieval]
  DB --> MR[Market retrieval]
  DB --> KR[Competitor retrieval]
  CR --> CA[Customer agent]
  MR --> MA[Market agent]
  KR --> KA[Competitor agent]
  CA --> WF[Bounded council state machine]
  MA --> WF
  KA --> WF
  DB --> MOD[Moderator]
  DB --> J[Judge]
  MOD --> WF
  J --> WF
  BACK --> WF
  WF --> REQ[Versioned provisional requirements]
  REQ --> REVIEW[Human review / rationale]
  REVIEW --> AUD[(Append-only audit events)]
  REVIEW --> PDF[PDF report]
```

## User journey

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Choose series / market / derivative / horizon] --> B[Describe goals]
  B --> C[Confirm analysis scope]
  C --> D[Overview and vehicle areas]
  D --> E[Explore specialist evidence]
  E --> F[Start council]
  F --> G[Perspectives]
  G --> H[One challenge round]
  H --> I[Judge assessment]
  I --> J[At most one clarification]
  J --> K[Provisional proposal]
  K --> L[Human review]
  L --> M[Approve / reject / defer / request evidence]
  L --> N[Edit or challenge]
  N --> K
  M --> O[Export report and audit]
```

## Implementation choices

The initial application uses a local-first Vite React TypeScript SPA. This is an intentional lightweight alternative to the recommended Next.js stack because the prototype needs no server rendering. React Three Fiber, Three.js and Drei provide the vehicle viewer and agent sculptures. Recharts handles interactive charts, Zustand owns serializable state, and jsPDF generates an actual downloadable PDF. CSS design tokens and a small reusable UI layer keep the visual system consistent without importing a large component catalog. Routes use React Router; static hosting must rewrite non-asset URLs to index.html.

The application uses one visible 3D canvas at a time, capped device pixel ratio, suspended animation when hidden, reduced-motion support, and a 2D fallback. Approved GLB assets can replace a clearly identified conceptual procedural vehicle. No generated shape is represented as an accurate BMW. A BMW roundel is omitted until a legitimate supplied or appropriately licensed asset is available; text branding identifies the concept.

## Entity contracts

| Entity | Key fields and invariants |
|---|---|
| AnalysisScope | vehicle, market, powertrain, planningHorizon, prompt, confirmedAt; a session freezes its scope |
| Evidence | id, domain, source title, source location, publication date, vehicle/market/powertrain, passage, category, type, provenance, quantitative metadata, exclusion reason |
| Finding | id, statement, topic, evidenceIds, uncertainty; identifies distinct records and observations |
| Requirement | id, scope, topic, description, findingIds, evidenceIds, criterion values, priority rationale, evidence strength, assumptions, uncertainty, impact, risk, effort, alternatives, status, version, history |
| CouncilEvent | event ID, sequence, stage, actor, visible statement, evidenceIds, assumptions, timestamp; never hidden model reasoning |
| Decision | requirementId, expectedVersion, action, rationale, actor, timestamp; approval is specific to a version |
| AuditEvent | id, ISO timestamp, actor, action, requirementId/version, before, after, evidenceIds, rationale |
| Scenario | id, label, weights, assumptions; deterministic sensitivity exercise, not a sales forecast |

Example evidence envelope:

```ts
interface QuantitativeClaim {
  numerator: number;
  denominator: number;
  unit: 'unique-records' | 'unique-customers' | 'study-responses' | 'vehicles';
  sourceId: string;
  filters: Record<string, string>;
  market: string;
  period: string;
  method: string;
  limitations: string[];
}
```

## Integration responsibilities

| Team module | Integration point | Production responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| Data engineering | lib/types, lib/api | Ingest provided XLSX/PDF privately; deduplicate classification rows using source IDs; retain lineage and permissions |
| Customer RAG | IntelligenceService.listEvidence | Enforce customer-domain retrieval with backend credentials and authorization |
| Market RAG | IntelligenceService.listEvidence | Distinguish 2024/2025 observations from supplied 2030 future figures; retain dates and units |
| Competitor RAG | IntelligenceService.listEvidence | Verify model, trim, market, availability, date and source URL; no unsupported cross-market comparisons |
| Agent orchestration | IntelligenceService.streamCouncil | Emit ordered typed events; enforce one challenge round, optional single clarification, duration/token limits, cancellation |
| Product backend | requirement read/write and decision methods | Optimistic concurrency, immutable version approval, transactional audit writes and idempotency |
| Frontend | components, pages, store | Rendering, navigation, filters, evidence drilldowns, deliberate human review, accessible 3D controls |
| Reporting | lib/export | Render one consistent snapshot with current scope, scores, evidence exclusions, scenarios and audit |

Suggested HTTP mapping: GET /analyses/:id/evidence; GET /analyses/:id/requirements; POST /analyses/:id/councils; GET /councils/:id/events (SSE); POST /councils/:id/control; PATCH /requirements/:id with expectedVersion; POST /requirements/:id/decisions; POST /evidence/:id/exclusions; GET /analyses/:id/audit. Backend errors must distinguish unavailable data, access denied, version conflict, timeout and validation errors. A disconnect must not silently repeat a decision or council stage.

## Deterministic prioritization

Criteria are bounded 0–5 assessments: observed need, severity, competitive gap, future relevance and feasibility (ease). The displayed priority is `100 * sum(knownWeight * criterion / 5) / sum(knownWeight)`. Unknown inputs are excluded from the weighted sum, coverage is shown, and all unknown inputs or zero active weight produces an unknown score. Evidence strength is shown independently; weak evidence triggers review rather than quietly becoming a fabricated business score. Rough effort is qualitative. Weight changes update rankings and append an audit event. Scenario presets express PM preferences, not probabilities or predictions.

## Council state machine

States: idle → topic → perspectives → challenge → assessment → revision → proposal → review. Revision is the single optional clarification slot and explicitly records whether used. Pause and interruption retain the current stage. Resume continues from that stage. Review is terminal for one run; reopening creates a separately traceable run. A timer advances only while running; a maximum duration and fixed event list bound processing. User challenges pause processing and are logged with a rationale. Real inference later must obey the same controller and typed events.

## Persistence and security

Browser localStorage stores a versioned demo session, PM review states, scores and audit history; it is editable local convenience storage and is not a secure immutable production audit database. Corrupt or incompatible browser state is recoverable with a fresh demo session. Confidential data must never enter public fixtures, committed files, client-side secrets or public asset folders. Production authentication, authorization, domain retrieval restrictions, database durability and audit immutability belong to backend services.

## Asset and design policy

Inspect 21st.dev for inspiration and document any adopted code with the exact license. Prefer original small components and procedural geometry when a catalog requires a paid service or credentials. Do not install account-level MCP configuration or request paid subscriptions simply to finish the prototype. Track asset provenance in ASSETS.md. Any model replacement must have a verified redistribution/license grant. Neither trademark imagery nor external models are presumed licensed by availability alone.

## Acceptance and verification

- Home scope controls persist into every page; electric-only topics are filtered from combustion derivatives.
- Every major route renders at desktop and mobile sizes, including direct links and browser history.
- Viewer supports orbit, zoom, reset, reduced motion and WebGL failure; labels do not claim exact model coordinates for a fallback.
- All five agent sculptures respond to typed agent states; one active stage drives the council visualization and visible evidence.
- Debate start/pause/resume/interrupt/challenge/review operate without unbounded loops or automatic PM approval.
- Evidence filters and search alter real fixture results, source drilldowns disclose denominator and limitations, and exclusions require a reason.
- Decisions require a rationale, significant edits increment version and invalidate approval, reopening is logged, and unknown scores remain unknown.
- Scenario sliders and presets update deterministic rankings, with a risk/impact chart and visible assumptions.
- Export creates a readable multi-page PDF containing scope, requirements, evidence, decisions, assumptions, scenario comparison and audit.
- Type checking, production build, domain tests and browser flow checks pass; limitations are recorded in README.

## Delivery sequence

1. Inspect repository and preserve useful code.
2. Create this complete PROJECT_SPEC.md before frontend edits.
3. Establish design tokens, typography, layout and navigation.
4. Implement the immersive homepage and vehicle viewer.
5. Implement five procedural agent entities and an avatar-state showcase.
6. Connect deterministic council orchestration and readable evidence panels.
7. Build customer, market and competitor intelligence views.
8. Build requirement review, scenarios, audit and real PDF export.
9. Verify code, runtime, visual behavior, routing and output; document integration and remaining limitations.

## Open questions

1. Which approved G60 (and F70/G70) GLB assets and BMW brand assets may the team redistribute?
2. Where will confidential datasets be hosted and which data-use/privacy restrictions apply?
3. Which source columns identify a unique observation or customer across duplicate classifications?
4. What units, regional definitions and provenance apply to supplied 2030 sales figures?
5. Which models, trims, model years and sources are approved for competitor comparisons?
6. What rubric, thresholds and consequential-uncertainty rules will PMs validate?
7. Which derivative combinations are available for each market and generation?
8. Which backend host, identity provider, RAG stores and streaming transport will the team choose?
9. What report retention, export access and audit retention policies apply?
10. Which topic should the live hackathon demo prioritize after real data is ingested?

## Collaboration and completion criteria

Use an understandable modular folder structure, typed contracts and a setup README. Keep presentation, fixtures, API adapters, scoring, orchestration, auditing and persistence separate. Do not commit or push unless explicitly instructed. MVP deliverables are this specification, the premium local frontend, the five agent entities, bounded council workflow, all major pages, a real PDF exporter, and honest limitations. No real AI inference, verified market forecast, production security, or accurate BMW model is implied by completing the mock-driven prototype.
'''

---

# BMW NEXT — AI Product Intelligence

An unofficial BMW challenge prototype: choose a vehicle and market, inspect source-linked evidence, watch a bounded AI council discussion, compare priorities, record version-specific human decisions, and export a real PDF.

Read [PROJECT_SPEC.md](PROJECT_SPEC.md) for the complete product specification, system architecture, user journey, team contracts and open questions. The original project introduction above is retained from the teammate's Entire README commit.

## Run locally

Use Node.js 22.12+ (tested with Node 25.7) and npm.

```bash
npm ci
npm run dev
```

Open the Local URL printed by Vite (normally http://127.0.0.1:5173). No API keys, paid services, database, login, or confidential dataset is needed. The dev server binds to loopback. To share a demo across devices, deliberately configure an appropriate host and access policy.

```bash
npm run build       # TypeScript checks and production bundle in dist/
npm run preview     # Serve that production build locally
npm test            # Domain logic, state machine, review/version and PDF tests
npm run test:e2e    # Five end-to-end browser workflows, desktop and mobile
npm run format      # Format source, tests and configuration
```

Browser tests use an installed Google Chrome via Playwright's `chrome` channel. Install Chrome, or change the channel and install Playwright Chromium with `npx playwright install chromium`. The tests use an isolated browser profile and enable software WebGL for machines without a GPU. The Playwright configuration starts or reuses the local development server. Screenshots, traces and downloaded PDFs go to ignored `test-results/`.

For static hosting, serve `dist/` and rewrite non-file routes to `index.html`. No production deployment is configured.

## Demo walkthrough

1. Select F70 / G60 / G70, market, available demo powertrain, a 3–5-year horizon and an optional goal. Confirm the scope. F70 currently offers combustion in the demo; other derivative/market availability is an integration question.
2. Use Overview's category controls to explore requirements and their sources. The concept sedan supports mouse/touch orbit, zoom, auto-rotation and reset. With viewer focus, arrow keys orbit and +/- zoom.
3. Explore customer feedback search and filters, synthetic satisfaction samples, market sensitivity controls and hypothetical competitor comparisons. Click sources for passages, dates, source location, calculation inputs and limitations.
4. Start the council. Its fixed sequence has three perspectives, one challenge round, one clarification, an assessment, proposal and PM review. Pause, resume, interrupt, challenge or expand the discussion. The Avatars studio previews the shared visual states.
5. Compare scenario presets and adjust weights. Review a requirement with a rationale: approve, reject, edit, challenge, defer, request evidence or reopen. Editing creates a new version and clears prior approval. Excluding evidence reopens linked requirements.
6. Inspect Audit Trail, then use Export report on any workspace page to download a multi-page PDF with the current scope, requirements, scoring, scenarios, sources, assumptions, council statements and audit history.

The demo initializes provisional requirements so all pages can be explored immediately. Council proposals revisit those seeded requirements rather than inventing new runtime content. Free-text goals and challenges are recorded, but do not invoke actual AI inference.

## Structure and integration points

```text
src/
  components/
    vehicle/        GLB viewer, studio lighting, controls and static fallback
    agents/         Five procedural sculptures and typed animation states
    council/        One scene containing all five entities
    dashboard/      Navigation and source explorer
    charts/         Risk/impact visualization
    requirements/   Human review and editing
    ui/             Shared controls, dialogs, motion and error boundary
  pages/            Home and seven workspace views
  lib/
    types/          Scope, evidence, findings, requirement, decision and audit contracts
    api/            IntelligenceService, demo adapter and production extension contract
    mock-data/      Explicitly synthetic fixtures; no private data
    scoring/        Deterministic priorities, coverage and scenario weights
    council/        Bounded deterministic state machine and visible scripted statements
    audit/          Structured event construction
    export/         Snapshot-based PDF generation
  store/            Zustand state, browser persistence and domain mutations
```

- **Data/retrieval teammates:** replace synthetic ingestion in `lib/api/service.ts`. Keep source IDs, locations, dates, deduplication units and quantitative denominators intact. Original feedback repeated across classification rows must not become additional observations.
- **Agent teammates:** implement the `IntelligenceService` streaming contract. `CouncilEvent` represents publishable discussion output, not private chain-of-thought. Backend orchestration must enforce the stage sequence, limits, cancellation and retrieval-domain authorization. The mock currently buffers its finite event list before timed playback; production SSE must be consumed incrementally with reconnect/idempotency handling.
- **Backend teammates:** implement authenticated analysis/requirement/evidence persistence with optimistic version checks and transactional append-only audit writes. The extended production service contract documents the required operations. Do not rely on client-side role filters to restrict agent retrieval.
- **Frontend teammates:** use `useAppStore` selectors and the shared domain types. Keep calculations in `lib/scoring`, workflow transitions in `lib/council`, and components focused on rendering/interactions.
- **3D teammates:** supply approved model assets to `VehicleViewer.modelUrl`, set the correct orientation and scale, then add spatial hotspots in verified coordinates. Asset and design provenance is in [ASSETS.md](ASSETS.md).

Suggested HTTP/SSE routes are documented in PROJECT_SPEC.md. Keep the backend technology interchangeable; FastAPI, a relational store and domain-specific retrieval are planned interfaces, not installed services.

## What is real and what is simulated

| Working now | Current limit / next integration |
|---|---|
| Responsive routes, accessible dialogs and keyboard controls | No authentication or server deployment |
| PBR GLB studio with orbit/zoom/reset and reduced-motion behavior | CC0 unbranded concept sedan; **not an accurate BMW**. Selection changes analysis scope, not the placeholder geometry |
| Five animated procedural agent entities | No voice or live model inference; hidden/offscreen vehicle animation is paused |
| Deterministic bounded council with pause/resume and audit | Scripted statements; challenges are retained but do not produce dynamic responses |
| Feedback drilldowns and explicit study sample calculations | All passages, study ratings, market curves and competitor patterns are synthetic |
| Deterministic scoring and scenario comparison | Rubric ratings, impact, risk and effort need real validation; no ROI or sales uplift is claimed |
| Human decisions, requirement versions and local audit | Versioned browser localStorage only; not shared or tamper-proof backend persistence |
| Actual downloadable PDF with pagination | Uses built-in Helvetica; extended writing systems need an embedded Unicode font in production |

Evidence strength is separate from priority. Unknown scores remain unknown; known-input weight coverage is visible. Approval is attached to one version. Browser reload pauses any active council for deliberate resumption. Starting a new analysis replaces the previous locally saved demo; export first if you want its report.

Google Fonts is the only optional remote display dependency; system fonts are used if unavailable. Vehicle textures are embedded in the locally bundled GLB, and the lighting has no external HDR dependency. Unsupported WebGL or an asset loading error produces a labelled static fallback. The production bundle lazy-loads 3D, analytics and PDF modules; Three.js remains the largest chunk (about 1.3 MB before gzip), as expected for this interactive prototype.

## Verification

The automated suite covers:

- Unknown-aware scoring, deterministic weighted means and zero-weight handling.
- Powertrain-appropriate topics and source/finding lineage.
- Bounded stage order, duration cap and pause/interruption behavior.
- Required rationales, stale-version rejection, edit invalidation and evidence exclusions.
- A valid multi-page PDF generated from the same application snapshot.
- Browser orbit/zoom/reset, scope confirmation, source filters, specialist routes, all council controls, review/version/exclusion, scenario weights, reload persistence, audit, PDF download, mobile navigation and deep links.

The exported PDF is additionally rendered for visual inspection. Dependency installation after the security updates reports zero known advisories. `npm run build` reports a large Three.js chunk warning; it is documented rather than hidden. There are no configured live AI/backend environment variables to verify.

Yes—**the current agents are scripted demos**. Your task is to replace the competitor demo with a real, evidence-grounded agent, then make the competitor page and council use that same agent.

Since **one team laptop will run everything**, I recommend one backend, one Ollama installation, and one shared Qwen model. Each agent gets a different role, its own evidence tools, and separate conversation history.

**What I found in your data**

There is **no dedicated competitor specification dataset** in that folder. There is a useful BMW baseline:

| Supplied data | What it supports |
|---|---|
| F70, G60 and G70 feedback | Customer experiences, complaints, strengths and occasional comparisons with rivals |
| Customer studies | BMW satisfaction measurements by vehicle and region |
| BMW option-list PDFs | What BMW already offers, including standard versus optional equipment |
| Sales workbook | Regional context, with 2024/2025 columns and a separate 2030 outlook |
| Briefing and reference slides | Requirements, traceability, prioritization and human review |

The feedback needs careful handling:

| File | Data rows | Distinct feedback IDs |
|---|---:|---:|
| F70 | 4,076 | 2,128 |
| G60 | 5,005 | 4,000 |
| G70 | 4,690 | 4,000 |

An ID can appear several times because one comment has several classifications. **We must preserve those classifications without counting them as separate customers.**

Other important constraints:

- A customer mentioning Tesla or Audi is evidence of their **perception**, not verified competitor specifications.
- The equipment lists are German-market documents dated July 2026. They cannot automatically establish US or Chinese availability.
- China’s G68 should remain distinguishable from G60.
- The studies contain different formats—EU/China means versus US response distributions. We should not average them together blindly.
- The 2030 sales column must remain future context, not observed sales.

The briefing explicitly permits external competitor research and emphasizes evidence, uncertainty and product-manager control. [BMW briefing](</Users/shaur/TUM/BMWHack/BMW_Hackathon_Briefing_Short.pdf>)

**What your competitor agent should actually optimize**

I would define its role as:

> “Advocate for BMW’s competitive advantage. Identify where comparable rivals set expectations, where BMW has meaningful differentiation, and which improvements could strengthen BMW’s position. Support factual claims with sources and challenge proposals that merely copy competitors.”

That gives it a deliberately narrow viewpoint. It is **BMW’s competitive strategist**, rather than an agent trying to help Mercedes defeat BMW.

Its “selfish” priorities would be:

- Close important competitive disadvantages.
- Protect existing BMW strengths.
- Find differentiation beyond feature parity.
- Challenge expensive features that add little competitive value.
- Identify how easily a rival could imitate a proposed advantage.

It should still acknowledge downsides and change its position when challenged with better evidence.

**The proposed agent workflow**

1. **Understand the comparison.**  
   Read vehicle, market, powertrain, planning horizon and topic. Select genuinely comparable vehicles; record why each belongs in the comparison.

2. **Check BMW’s current baseline.**  
   Retrieve the relevant option-list passages. Establish whether a capability already exists, is optional, varies by trim, or remains unknown. This prevents recommending existing equipment as a new innovation.

3. **Retrieve competitor evidence.**  
   Search a curated collection of official product pages, brochures and manuals first. Add dated reviews for usability evidence. Every record retains its URL/file, passage, publication date, market, model year and trim.

4. **Build the comparison in code.**  
   Normalize equipment into `standard`, `optional`, `unavailable`, `announced`, or `unknown`. Missing evidence must produce **unknown**, never “competitor does not have it.”

5. **Choose what to investigate next.**  
   Qwen can request another source, inspect a conflicting claim, or refine the comparison. The backend executes the permitted tools and returns the results.

6. **Generate competing options.**  
   For a gap, propose alternatives such as improving the existing interaction, matching a rival, or creating a different experience. Include a “keep the current approach” option when defensible.

7. **Validate and publish a structured result.**  
   Check that citations exist, comparisons match the scope, and predictions are labelled as hypotheses. Unsupported recommendations remain provisional.

This is what makes it **agentic**: it can choose evidence-gathering actions and revise its answer after seeing their results. Ollama supports this tool-call → application executes tool → model receives result loop. [Ollama tool calling](https://docs.ollama.com/capabilities/tool-calling)

For the first version, I would allow a small tool set:

```text
get_bmw_baseline
search_competitor_evidence
read_source
compare_equipment
find_conflicting_evidence
```

Keep the loop bounded—for example, three research rounds and a fixed tool-call budget. Start with a curated source collection; unrestricted live browsing can come later.

**How the positive and negative effects should appear**

Each recommendation should separate three things:

| Layer | Example |
|---|---|
| Evidence | A cited source establishes a competitor capability |
| Interpretation | The agent considers that capability a competitive expectation |
| Possible effect | BMW could reduce perceived inconvenience by improving its alternative |

A recommendation card could show:

- **Proposed change:** what BMW should improve.
- **Competitive benefit:** why it could strengthen BMW’s position.
- **Possible downside:** complexity, weak differentiation, imitation risk or another trade-off.
- **If BMW does nothing:** the potential competitive exposure.
- **Alternative:** a smaller or different intervention.
- **Evidence and uncertainty:** what is established and what needs testing.
- **Validation:** how a product manager could test the hypothesis.

We should not invent “+12% sales” or “−20% churn.” Without a validated causal model, effects remain qualitative hypotheses.

**How everyone’s agents connect**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    UI[Specialist pages and Agent Council] --> API[Shared backend]
    API --> Coordinator[Council coordinator]
    Coordinator --> Customer[Customer agent]
    Coordinator --> Market[Market agent]
    Coordinator --> Competitor[Competitor agent]
    Coordinator --> Moderator[Moderator agent]
    Coordinator --> Judge[Judge agent]
    Customer --> Qwen[One Ollama / Qwen runtime]
    Market --> Qwen
    Competitor --> Qwen
    Moderator --> Qwen
    Judge --> Qwen
    API <--> Store[Evidence, proposals, events and decisions]
```

**An agent is not a separate model installation.** It is the model plus a role, tools, evidence and conversation state.

| Agent | Primary responsibility |
|---|---|
| Customer | Customer needs, usability, pain points and strengths to preserve |
| Market | Regional relevance and future assumptions |
| Competitor | Competitive gaps, differentiation and imitation risk |
| Moderator | Frame the question, identify disagreements and request clarification |
| Judge | Assess evidence quality, consistency and unresolved uncertainty |

The **coordinator is ordinary backend code**. It controls whose turn it is and enforces limits. The moderator can guide the discussion, but should not control an unrestricted loop.

All teammates should implement the same interface:

```ts
runAgent({
  analysisId,
  proposalId,
  scope,
  stage,
  evidenceIds,
  priorPositions,
  challenge
}) => AgentResult
```

The shared result needs:

```text
agentId, runId, proposalId, proposalVersion
position: support | oppose | revise | insufficient_evidence
claims and supporting evidenceIds
recommendations
positiveEffects and negativeEffects
assumptions and uncertainties
challenges to other positions
short rationale
```

Use a shared JSON Schema and validate responses server-side. Ollama supports schema-constrained structured output; valid JSON still needs factual and citation checks. [Structured outputs](https://docs.ollama.com/capabilities/structured-outputs)

**How a real council session would work**

1. Moderator frames one proposal and its scope.
2. Customer, market and competitor agents produce independent initial positions.
3. Those positions are revealed to the group.
4. Moderator selects substantive disagreements.
5. Relevant agents respond to challenges using cited evidence.
6. Judge assesses support, contradictions and missing information.
7. Agents get one bounded revision round.
8. Moderator summarizes the proposal, alternatives and remaining disagreement.
9. The product manager approves, edits, rejects or requests evidence.

The council should be allowed to finish with **disagreement**. Forced consensus would hide useful information.

Initial positions should be independent to reduce agents simply echoing the first response. On one laptop, requests can run sequentially while keeping their histories separate.

**What the pages would look like**

The competitor page becomes a working research surface:

- **Scope and coverage:** selected BMW, peers, markets, source dates and missing evidence.
- **Comparison matrix:** sourced equipment and experience comparisons.
- **Opportunity cards:** recommendations with benefits, downsides and alternatives.
- **Activity feed:** “Checking BMW baseline,” “Comparing equipment,” “Validating sources.”
- **Actions:** Run analysis, inspect evidence, challenge a recommendation, send it to council.

The council opens the **same proposal ID and version** shown on the competitor page. It should not generate a disconnected second recommendation.

Likewise, each specialist page displays its own agent’s analysis. The council displays how those positions change after debate. A browser refresh should retrieve the stored result rather than run the model again.

**Does everyone need the same Qwen model?**

Not technically, but **yes, I recommend it for your hackathon**. Use the same exact model build, quantization, context settings, generation settings and comparable response budgets. Roles and evidence access differ deliberately.

That improves comparability; it does not eliminate bias. Five roles using one model can share the same blind spots, so the judge still needs deterministic validation and human review.

I would start by benchmarking **`qwen3:8b`** on the demo laptop, then choose a smaller or larger variant based on memory and measured latency. Pin the chosen model digest rather than relying on a changing default tag. [Ollama Qwen3 8B](https://ollama.com/library/qwen3:8b)

Teammates can develop against their own local setup, but the final demo should use the shared configuration. Only the backend talks to Ollama; the browser talks to the backend.

**The implementation order I recommend**

1. **Agree on shared contracts first:** evidence records, proposals, agent results and council events. Give one teammate ownership of shared integration files.
2. **Build your competitor agent independently:** ingestion, BMW baseline, curated competitor sources, tools, Qwen calls and validation.
3. **Connect the competitor page:** replace the fabricated peers and row-based strengths with actual stored results.
4. **Connect the council:** replace scripted statements and timer-driven playback with real backend events.
5. **Test one complete scenario:** one BMW series, one market, two verified peers and a few topics—through research, challenge, revision and human decision.

For your branch, I would own the competitor module, its evidence tools, tests and competitor page. Other teammates own their respective modules. Everyone imports the shared contract rather than editing separate versions of the council logic.

**The best first deliverable is one real competitor recommendation that survives a council challenge and remains traceable to its sources.** That establishes the complete working pattern before expanding to every vehicle and market. I’ve only inspected and planned here; no agent implementation or private-data import has been made yet.

**Your agent’s goal:** identify how BMW can compete better—what to improve, what to preserve, and where to differentiate.

**Planned workflow:**

1. **Read the scope:** BMW model, market, powertrain and feature/topic.
2. **Check BMW’s baseline:** use the supplied equipment PDFs and relevant customer comparisons.
3. **Research comparable rivals:** retrieve official specifications, brochures, manuals and configurators. Starting sources: [Tesla manuals](https://www.tesla.com/ownersmanual/model3/en_us/), [Mercedes brochures](https://www.mercedes-benz.co.uk/passengercars/ebrochure-download.html), [BYD regional product pages](https://www.byd.com/uk).
4. **Verify the comparison:** match country, model year and trim; distinguish standard, optional and announced features. Save the source passage and date. Missing information stays **unknown**.
5. **Investigate gaps:** Qwen chooses tools to retrieve more evidence or check contradictions, then revises its assessment. **That tool-and-feedback loop makes it agentic.**
6. **Recommend:** show the proposed improvement, competitive benefit, possible downside, alternative, citations and uncertainty. Predicted effects stay hypotheses—not invented sales figures.
7. **Publish and debate:** the competitor page displays that result; the council challenges the **same proposal**, and your agent defends or revises it using evidence.

**Start small:** one BMW series, one market, two comparable rivals and three feature areas. Curate reliable sources first, then add controlled live research. Qwen interprets the evidence; it must not serve as the source of competitor facts.

**How quickly?** A narrow working version is roughly a few hours of implementation and testing; comprehensive competitor coverage takes longer. We should benchmark Qwen immediately before promising debate response times.

+# BMW NEXT backend scaffold
+
+This is the first file/contract scaffold on `Competitors_Agent`. It starts a
+FastAPI server and exposes draft schemas in `/docs`. It does **not** ingest data,
+run competitor research, generate recommendations, or conduct a live debate yet.
+The existing frontend still uses its explicit demo adapter.
+
+## Start from the repository root
+
+Python 3.11+:
+
+```bash
+python3 -m venv backend/.venv
+source backend/.venv/bin/activate
+python -m pip install -r backend/requirements.txt
+cp backend/.env.example backend/.env
+python -m uvicorn backend.main:app --reload --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --env-file backend/.env
+```
+
+- API documentation: http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs
+- Scaffold status: http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/health
+- Frontend remains separately started with `npm run dev`.
+
+The env example points to the supplied BMW data folder. Change it on other team
+laptops. No source data is copied into the repository. Local env files, Python
+environments and generated private evidence indexes must stay untracked.
+
+Ollama is **not needed to start this scaffold**. Later, install/run Ollama and
+pull the agreed Qwen model. All agents will share `OLLAMA_BASE_URL` and
+`OLLAMA_MODEL`. The provisional model is `qwen3:8b`; benchmark and pin the exact
+model build with the team before integration. The adapter in `llm/ollama.py`
+implements an explicit chat call but is not called by any scaffold route.
+
+## Ownership and layout
+
+```text
+backend/
+  main.py                 FastAPI app and scaffold health endpoint
+  config.py               Shared environment settings
+  agents/
+    base.py               Interface every teammate implements
+    competitor.py         Competitor role and future execution loop
+  tools/
+    evidence.py           BMW baseline, source retrieval and comparison contracts
+  schemas/
+    common.py             Scope and proposal/version references
+    evidence.py           Source provenance and equipment availability
+    agent.py              Claims, effects, recommendations and debate positions
+    council.py            Explicit PM debate request
+  llm/ollama.py           Shared Ollama chat adapter
+  council/coordinator.py  Bounded council orchestration entry point
+  api/
+    competitor.py         Standalone analysis endpoint
+    council.py            Separate PM-triggered debate endpoint
+```
+
+Competitor owner: `agents/competitor.py`, competitor evidence implementation and
+`api/competitor.py`. Teammates add their own role modules implementing `Agent`.
+Agree on changes to `schemas/`, `llm/`, `main.py` and `council/` before merging.
+Python contracts currently use snake_case; the frontend uses camelCase. Add an
+explicit HTTP adapter (or agree a common wire naming convention) when integrating.
+
+## Endpoints and current behavior
+
+| Route | Current behavior |
+| --- | --- |
+| `GET /api/health` | Reports scaffold state; does not claim Ollama is connected |
+| `POST /api/competitor/analyze` | Validates analysis input, then returns HTTP 501 |
+| `POST /api/council/debate` | Requires `trigger: "pm_requested"` and a proposal version, then returns HTTP 501 |
+
+Analysis never calls the coordinator. The PM's **Debate this proposal** button
+will call the debate endpoint explicitly. The trigger field is a workflow
+contract, not authentication; add real PM authorization before shared deployment.
+The coordinator will also need persistence, stale-version checks, idempotency,
+pause/cancel, bounded tool/turn budgets and real progress events before it is live.
+
+Example analysis body for `/docs`:
+
+```json
+{
+  "analysis_id": "analysis-001",
+  "scope": {
+    "vehicle": "G60",
+    "market": "Europe",
+    "powertrain": "Electric",
+    "horizon": 4,
+    "topic": "Displays"
+  },
+  "stage": "analysis"
+}
+```
+
+## Next implementation steps
+
+1. Read the supplied data in place; preserve exact sheet/cell and PDF page
+   locations. Deduplicate feedback by ID while preserving category assignments.
+2. Curate dated, region/trim-specific competitor source records. German BMW
+   equipment lists do not establish US/China availability; keep G68 distinct.
+3. Implement `EvidenceTools`, then a bounded Qwen research loop. Validate all

+    @classmethod

+        try:


A successful response contains claims, recommendations, positive/negative
hypothetical effects, alternatives, uncertainties, cited evidence records and a
research activity log. Read it again at `/api/competitor/runs/{run_id}`. The log
records retrieval actions, not private reasoning. A run may take several minutes
on a laptop; it has a 360-second total budget and a 120-second per-model-call
timeout, configurable in `.env`. A failed run is never replaced with fake results.

## How it works

1. Search equipment, feedback and official competitor records for the topic.
2. Qwen chooses additional searches or source reads (three rounds, six tool calls
   maximum). Retrieval is restricted to the request's BMW model, market and known
   powertrain. It can search for counterexamples as well as supporting evidence.
3. Request schema-constrained JSON. Check citation IDs against evidence actually
   retrieved, role identity, unique claim IDs, hypothetical effects, and debate
   target IDs. Permit one repair; reject output that still fails.
4. Mark missing official competitor/BMW baseline coverage as insufficient evidence.
   Persist the result and its evidence snapshot locally for consistent reuse.

Citation validation checks provenance and scope, **not semantic truth**. Review
interpretations and compare original documents before product decisions. Results
are conditional recommendations, not approved requirements or proven forecasts.

## Evidence and limitations

- `ingest.py` reads the three feedback workbooks and option-list PDFs in place.
  Classification duplicates are merged by feedback ID, exact comment, country and
  powertrain; categories and original cell locators are retained. It does not
  compute representative frequency estimates from this selected feedback.
- PDF excerpts retain page/character locations. Table symbols/trim columns and
  rotated text are not reliably decoded. The German July 2026 lists do not
  establish US/China fitment, and equipment availability still needs visual review.
- `evidence/competitors.json` contains **three small human-curated official-source
  summaries**: Tesla Model 3 US rear-screen controls, Mercedes E-Class US 2024
  Superscreen, and BYD SEAL UK 2026 touchscreen. Country/year/trim caveats are
  retained. This is starter coverage, not a complete competitor database.
- Runtime research searches this catalog; it does not crawl the internet. Extend
  the catalog using `EvidenceRecord` fields and original official links, then
  rebuild. Do not label customer speculation as official competitor equipment.
- Sales and customer-study workbooks are not ingested by this first version.
  G68 remains distinct from G60; no G68 data is silently merged.
- `backend/data/` holds private indexes and runs and is gitignored. Raw source
  data, local `.env`, model files and Python environments must stay untracked.

## Team integration

`agents/base.py` defines `run(AgentRequest) -> AgentResult`. Teammates implement
that interface for their roles and share `schemas/` and `llm/ollama.py`.
The competitor implementation accepts internal perspective/challenge/revision
requests with proposal/version and actual peer claims. It resolves known peer
citations and marks unresolved ones unverified. It rejects invented challenge
targets. Council orchestration itself is still owned by the coordinator work.

The HTTP analysis route accepts standalone analysis only. The PM's **Debate this
proposal** button must call `/api/council/debate` explicitly with a proposal
version and `trigger: "pm_requested"`. This field is a workflow assertion, not
user authentication. Coordinator persistence, claim exchange, pause/cancel and
proposal version checks still need integration before a live council.

Wire the competitor page to the returned stored run; do not create independent
page/council copies. Python fields are snake_case, so add a frontend adapter for
its camelCase types. This backend currently assumes one local server worker and
allows one competitor run at a time (HTTP 409 when busy). It is a local demo
service, without authentication or multi-process job orchestration.

## Checks and errors

```bash
python -m unittest discover -s backend/tests -v
```

- 422: invalid input, scope/citation ID or debate sent to analysis.
- 409: a competitor run is already active.
- 503: evidence index or Ollama/model unavailable.
- 504: inference/run timed out.
- 502: invalid model output after a bounded repair.
- 501: council coordinator not implemented yet.

"""Persist job progress; inference stays on this single team laptop.

A server restart marks unfinished jobs interrupted. It never silently replays a
PM debate or pretends a partially generated result completed.
"""
import asyncio
import json
import logging
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from uuid import uuid4, UUID
from fastapi import APIRouter, HTTPException
from backend.config import Settings
from backend.runtime import run_lock

router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/jobs", tags=["Live jobs"])
tasks: dict[str, asyncio.Task] = {}

def path(job_id):
    return Settings.from_env().runs_dir / "jobs" / (str(UUID(str(job_id))) + ".json")

def save(job):
    p = path(job['id']); p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    temporary = p.with_suffix('.tmp'); temporary.write_text(json.dumps(job, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)); temporary.replace(p)

def read(job_id):
    job = json.loads(path(job_id).read_text())
    if job['status'] in ('queued', 'running') and str(job_id) not in tasks:
        job.update(status='failed', error='Server restarted during this run. Start a new run explicitly.', phase='Interrupted')
        save(job)
    return job

async def submit(kind, request, work):
    # No await between check and reservation: atomic within our single event loop.
    if run_lock.locked() or any(not t.done() for t in tasks.values()):
        raise HTTPException(409, 'Another live analysis or debate is running on this laptop.')
    job = dict(id=str(uuid4()), kind=kind, status='queued', phase='Queued', request=request,
               created_at=datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(), result=None, error=None)
    save(job)
    def progress(phase):
        job['phase'] = phase; save(job)
    async def execute():
        try:
            async with run_lock:
                job['status'] = 'running'; progress('Reading evidence')
                result = await work(progress)
                job.update(status='succeeded', phase='Complete', result=result.model_dump(mode='json'))
        except asyncio.CancelledError:
            job.update(status='failed', phase='Interrupted', error='Backend stopped during this run. Retry explicitly.')
            raise
        except Exception as exc:
            logging.getLogger(__name__).exception('Live %s job failed', kind)
            job.update(status='failed', phase='Failed', error=str(exc)[:700] or type(exc).__name__)
        finally:
            save(job); tasks.pop(job['id'], None)
    tasks[job['id']] = asyncio.create_task(execute())
    return job

@router.get('/{job_id}')
async def get_job(job_id: UUID):
    try: return read(job_id)
    except FileNotFoundError as exc: raise HTTPException(404, 'Job not found') from exc
EOF

import asyncio
from uuid import uuid4, UUID
from fastapi import HTTPException
from backend.config import Settings
from backend.schemas.council import DebateRequest, DebateResult, CouncilTurn
from backend.storage import RunStore
from backend.council.participants import PARTICIPANTS

STAGES = ('perspectives', 'challenge', 'revision', 'assessment', 'review')

def load_proposal(request, settings):
    try: source = RunStore(settings.runs_dir).read(request.source_run_id)
    except FileNotFoundError as exc: raise HTTPException(404, 'Saved competitor analysis not found') from exc
    if source.analysis_id != request.analysis_id or source.scope != request.scope:
        raise HTTPException(409, 'The saved analysis scope does not match this debate.')
    if request.proposal.proposal_id != source.run_id or request.proposal.version != 1:
        raise HTTPException(409, 'Proposal reference is stale. Use the immutable analysis run ID and version 1.')
    if source.model != settings.ollama_model:
        raise HTTPException(409, 'Analysis model differs from the shared council model. Rerun the analysis.')
    return source

async def start_debate(request: DebateRequest, repository, progress=lambda _:None, settings=None) -> DebateResult:
    settings = settings or Settings.from_env()
    source = load_proposal(request, settings)
    # Freshness must hold at debate time too, not only when analysis was created.
    sources = []
    for record in source.evidence:
        try: resolved = repository.read(record.id, source.scope)
        except ValueError as exc: raise HTTPException(409, 'Analysis evidence changed; rerun analysis.') from exc
        if resolved != record: raise HTTPException(409, 'Analysis evidence changed; rerun analysis.')
        if record.source_type == 'competitor_official' and not repository.is_current(record):
            raise HTTPException(409, 'Competitor evidence expired; refresh sources and rerun analysis.')
        sources.append(record)
    # Bound source context and retrieve customer counterevidence.
    for record in repository.search(source.scope.topic, source.scope, 'customer_feedback', limit=3):
        if record.id not in {r.id for r in sources}: sources.append(record)
    context = {'proposal':request.proposal.model_dump(), 'question':request.question,
               'scope':source.scope.model_dump(), 'recommendations':[r.model_dump() for r in source.recommendations],
               'limitations':source.uncertainties}
    turns = [CouncilTurn(agent_id='competitor',stage='perspectives',position=source.position)]
    # Assign globally stable references without modifying the persisted source.
    turns[0] = turns[0].model_copy(deep=True)
    for i,claim in enumerate(turns[0].position.claims): claim.id=f'competitor-perspectives-{i+1}'
    async with asyncio.timeout(720):
        for role in ('customer','market'):
            progress(f'{role.title()} agent: independent perspective')
            role_sources = [r for r in sources if (r.source_type == 'customer_feedback' if role == 'customer' else r.source_type == 'competitor_official')][:6]
            turns.append(await PARTICIPANTS[role](settings).turn('perspectives',context,role_sources,[]))
        progress('Customer agent: challenging the competitor position')
        turns.append(await PARTICIPANTS['customer'](settings).turn('challenge',context,sources,turns))
        progress('Competitor agent: responding and revising')
        turns.append(await PARTICIPANTS['competitor'](settings).turn('revision',context,sources,turns))
        progress('Judge: assessing disagreements and evidence')
        turns.append(await PARTICIPANTS['judge'](settings).turn('assessment',context,sources,turns))
    return DebateResult(run_id=str(uuid4()),source_run_id=source.run_id,analysis_id=source.analysis_id,
        proposal=request.proposal,scope=source.scope,question=request.question,model=settings.ollama_model,
        turns=turns,evidence=sources,limitations=[
        'Local Customer and Market Qwen role adapters are used; teammate implementations have not been merged.',
        'Market role has no sales or causal impact dataset and cannot estimate commercial success.',
        'BMW trim gaps remain unverified. AI grounding checks are fallible; PM review is required.',
        'One bounded challenge/revision round. No automatic feature approval.'])

|---|---|---|
| **BMW Group Report 2025**, pp. 9, 67, 77–78 | Regional deliveries for **2021–2025**, electrification trends and wider market growth | Mostly BMW Group-level, not individual model/feature demand |
| **sales_volumes.xlsx** | Regional comparison for F70, G60/G68 and G70, using 2024, 2025 and 2030 values | Only two historical years; G60/G68 combined; **no powertrain breakdown** |
| **Customer studies workbook** | Regional satisfaction and feature priorities across Europe, China and the US | A **2025 snapshot**, with different survey formats and no clear respondent counts |
| **Three feedback workbooks** | Customer concerns by country, model and powertrain | No date column, repeated classifications, uneven regional coverage |
| **Option lists, briefing and images** | Product baseline and project requirements | Not historical market-trend datasets |

**A real example already available:** the annual report says BMW Group deliveries increased **7.3% in Europe** but declined **12.5% in China** in 2025. It also reports BEV delivery growth of **3.6%** and PHEV growth of **20.0%**. These are usable market signals—with their original scope preserved. :codex-file-citation{path="/Users/shaur/TUM/BMWHack/BMW-Group-Report-2025-en.pdf" purpose="source"}

- Identifies regional growth and pressure.
- Explains changes in BMW’s electrification mix.
- Uses customer evidence to suggest priorities for investigation.
- Challenges council proposals that lack regional evidence.

The data layer is in place: it now imports the supplied sales workbook and combines it with dated BMW, ACEA and IEA evidence. Growth calculations run in Python, while Qwen chooses relevant evidence, looks for counterpoints and proposes a testable recommendation.

For the UI, I’m building a dark, animated signal dashboard with one main chart and expandable sources, so the evidence stays accessible without crowding the page.

The Market page uses a real local `qwen3:8b` agent and dated evidence, with no

digital experiences and regional demand. They do not imply that every announced
feature is popular, or that copying it will increase BMW sales.

## Run on the team laptop

From the repository root, follow the Python/Ollama setup in [README](README.md), then:


`localhost:5173` can resolve to a different project listening on IPv6.
`/api/market/status` reports model name, digest, Ollama address, readiness and
busy state. All roles share `OLLAMA_MODEL` and one inference lock. Run one backend
worker. A branch contains agent code; it does not run its own model server.

## Evidence and screen

The screen separates one selected industry signal, BMW Group regional context,
and model-volume inputs. Select Europe, China or the United States and a topic.
A single chart switches between Group history and supplied model inputs; 2030
is displayed separately as an assumption, never as observed history. Expanded
source sections include original links, periods, workbook cells and caveats.
Animations respect reduced-motion preferences; the layout supports mobile.

The checked-in `evidence/market.json` contains 13 curated records and nine signals,
reviewed on 10 October 2026. The importer adds nine model/region records from
`sales_volumes.xlsx` to the private, ignored `backend/data/market.json` index.
There are 22 records and 12 series after import. Source material:

- BMW Group Report 2025, supplied PDF: page 78 regional Group deliveries for
  2021–2025; page 77 global BEV/PHEV deliveries. Group includes BMW, MINI and
  Rolls-Royce. The regional table is rounded; calculated growth can differ from
  reported growth. Public entry: https://www.bmwgroup.com/en/report/2025/index.html
- `sales_volumes.xlsx`: F70, G60_G68 and G70, 2024/2025 inputs plus 2030 assumptions.

- BMW's January 2026 Alexa+ announcement: a planned digital experience, not measured
  rollout, uptake or satisfaction. The source URL and country limits are in the catalog.

Customer feedback is optional counterevidence from the existing private index.
Individual comments have no representative prevalence or market-share denominator.
The supplied customer studies are snapshots, not trend series, and are not ingested.

Sources are curated snapshots, not an autonomous news feed. To refresh, inspect
primary sources, update the catalog's exact measure, geography, period, limitations,
verification/review dates and signal fields, then rerun the importer. Industry
signals become ineligible after their review date (initially 9 November 2026).
Rebuilding an index alone does not renew source verification. Historical Group
series remain historical. Missing topic/region coverage is shown explicitly.

## Agent workflow

1. Read scoped, dated market evidence. Python calculates growth, not Qwen.
2. Qwen may search and read the catalog through two bounded research rounds, at most
   four calls. Tools cannot access arbitrary paths or URLs. Include available
   customer counterevidence and source limitations.
3. Produce one proposed investigation, possible benefit, risk, opposing argument
   and validation step. Facts select source IDs and are hydrated from source text.
   Generated interpretations are separate; benefits are hypotheses, not success rates.
4. Validate citation IDs and numeric assertions. A separate Qwen grounding review
   checks populations, periods and causality. Allow one repair, then fail visibly.
   Model interpretation and model review can still be wrong; PM review matters.
5. Save the immutable result and evidence snapshot. The browser retains the job
   UUID and selected filters. Reloading resumes the same job, without starting
   duplicate inference. Backend restarts mark unfinished jobs interrupted.

API: `GET /api/market/dashboard`, `GET /api/market/status`,
`POST /api/market/jobs`, `GET /api/market/runs/{run_id}`. Jobs use shared
`GET /api/jobs/{job_id}`. The standalone request adds `market_topic` to
`AgentRequest`; see `/docs` for the full schema.

## Council and team integration

**Bring to council** opens the saved proposal. Only the PM's **Start live debate**
button invokes the coordinator. It checks the saved scope, model, proposal version
and evidence freshness before inference. A Market-led debate has six turns:

1. Saved Market position.
2. Independent Customer position.
3. Independent Competitor position.
4. Customer challenges an actual Market claim by ID.
5. Market answers the challenged claim(s), conceding or defending with evidence.
6. Judge assesses the disagreement; the outcome awaits PM review.

For Competitor-led proposals the Market agent supplies an independent position
and the challenge. Market uses the same evidence agent in both paths. Stage-specific
JSON constraints prevent revisions from opening new challenges. Referenced claims
must exist, and revisions must answer all claims challenged against Market.
No automatic council run, feature approval, forecast uplift or commercial-success
probability is produced.

Customer, Competitor and Judge council adapters perform real local Qwen inference,
but teammates' separate implementations have not been merged into this branch.
Replace their factories in `backend/council/participants.py` with adapters exposing
`turn(stage, context, sources, prior) -> CouncilTurn`. Preserve source validation,
actual peer references, shared `Settings`/model and the PM trigger. Missing peer
coverage must yield an explicit limitation, not invented evidence. Both private
indexes are needed for the full council; standalone Market can run without the
customer/competitor index. Other platform pages still have demo data.

content.text:
**I checked, and I can’t honestly call the whole workflow verified yet.** There are important distinctions:

- **Real Qwen is connected:** the backend reports `ollama`, `qwen3:8b`, and 55 loaded sources. Your agents share this model; their code, prompts and evidence make them different agents.
- **Existing debates aren’t proof of the final integration:** all eight saved sessions use the older `legacy` participant runtime. They contain generated arguments, citations, challenges and replies, but don’t prove the current teammate handlers ran. New sessions are configured to use those handlers.
- **Voice has a gap:** ElevenLabs receives the actual saved assessment and requirements, but its `ask_jury` bridge is currently disabled. Voice replies therefore aren’t guaranteed to come from local Qwen.
- **Approval is separate:** discussing or saying “yes” doesn’t approve a requirement. The PM currently confirms it on **Decisions & scenarios**.
- **50 integration tests passed**, but they use controlled fixtures/mocks; that doesn’t establish real model performance.

The proper end-to-end acceptance check is:

1. **Start a fresh council** and verify `participant_runtime: native`, actual Ollama usage, and implementation names for each specialist.
2. **Inspect the debate:** each challenge must reference another agent’s specific claim, and its response must address that challenge—not repeat an opening statement.
3. **Trace citations:** open the cited dataset rows/passages and verify they support the claim.
4. **Trace the verdict:** match its assessment ID, proposed requirements and evidence to what the voice session receives.
5. **Test voice → Qwen → PM confirmation:** enable and verify the local Judge bridge, ask about an exact requirement, then explicitly confirm its version and verify the saved decision.

Also, the original Competitor branch had a scaffolded council coordinator; its current debate handler required integration code. So “every agent was copied unchanged” would be inaccurate.

**The next priority is proving a fresh native debate and closing the voice-to-Qwen gap—not more UI polish.**

I’ll start a fresh council using the real agents and local Qwen, record its runtime, and inspect the evidence, challenges, responses and final requirements. I’ll also connect and test the Judge’s voice-to-Qwen path. I’ll leave the advanced Moderator redesign for later, as you requested.
